paragraphs: Why do people get and keep things? Most people say the answer is simple. People get goods because they want to use them. The owner uses them, or his family uses them. In theory, the family is part of the owner. Many people think this is the only good reason in economics. They think the theory needs to look only at this reason. Using goods can help with the needs of the body, like comfort. It can also help with higher needs. These are needs of the mind, of the spirit or of beauty. Goods help with these higher needs in a less direct way, as all readers of economics know.

But this simple idea is not really true. Using goods is not the real reason why people always collect more. The real reason for owning things is the wish to be better than others. People want to compete. This wish started the idea of owning things. It is still active today. It also shapes all the parts of society that ownership touches. Having wealth gives a person honour. It makes him look better than other people. Using goods is not as strong a reason as this. No other reason is as strong, above all for collecting more and more wealth.

Of course, we must not forget one thing. In a society where almost all goods belong to someone, people must earn a living. For poorer people, this is a strong reason, and it is always there. Some people do hard work with their hands. They have very little, and they keep very little. Their life is never safe. For them, the need for food and comfort may be the main reason for some time. But later we will see something. Even for these poor people, this need is not as strong as some people think.

Now think of the people who mostly collect wealth. For them, the need for food or comfort is never an important reason. Ownership did not start because people needed the smallest amount to live. From the beginning, the main reason was the honour that wealth brings. It made the owner look better than others. Later, no other reason has taken its place, except for short times and in a few cases.

At first, property was booty. Booty means things that people took from enemies in a fight. People kept these things as signs of their win. At that time, the group often fought other groups. So the value of owned things or people came from a comparison. People compared the owner with the enemy who lost these things. Later, people started to see a difference between one person and his group. Early on, people also compared the owner with his less lucky neighbours in the group. This made the booty more valuable, but at first it was not the main reason. A man's strength was still the group's strength. The owner of the booty felt that he kept the honour of his group. Later societies also see brave acts in this way, above all the honours of war.
